title: Under the Banner of Heaven: A Story of Violent Faith
author: Jon Krakauer
target_audience: General readers interested in American religion and society
core_themes: History of Mormonism and its offshoots
Role of religion in American culture
primary_purpose: To investigate and contextualize a brutal double murder committed in the name of religious belief by examining the broader history of Mormonism, the rise of fundamentalist sects, and the cultural and psychological forces that can drive individuals to extremism.

structure_format.narrative_style: Blends investigative journalism, historical analysis, and narrative nonfiction.
structure_format.organization: Alternates between recounting the 1984 Lafferty murders and providing a historical overview of the Mormon faith—especially its fundamentalist branches.
features: Analysis of faith, psychology, and violence

key_concepts_lessons: Religious beliefs, when interpreted literally and without checks, can justify extreme actions.
The roots of religious violence often trace back to a mix of historical, psychological, and sociological factors.
Mormonism, like many American-born religions, has a complex history marked by schisms over doctrine and practice.
Charismatic leaders and insular communities can foster environments where radical ideologies take root.
Understanding religious violence requires acknowledging both faith's power to inspire good and its potential to justify atrocity.
notable_features: Exploration of Mormon history from its founding to modern times
Focus on real-life crime as a lens for broader themes
Critical yet balanced examination of faith
cultural_historical_context: Published in the early 2000s, at a time of increasing public interest in the intersection of religion and violence, especially post-9/11. The book brought attention to lesser-known aspects of American religious history and highlighted the persistence of fringe movements, particularly within Mormon fundamentalism.
reception_impact: Bestseller, critically acclaimed for its thorough research and narrative style
Generated strong reactions—praised for its courage, criticized by some for its portrayal of religion
Influenced public discussions on religious extremism
Inspired a television adaptation and extensive academic debate
Helped raise awareness about the challenges faced by women and children within polygamous and fundamentalist communities

The Family: The Secret Fundamentalism at the Heart of American Power by Jeff Sharlet
